name: UNBLOCS
question: Is thulium laser transurethral vaporesection of the prostate (ThuVARP) equivalent to TURP for symptom score and urinary flow rate 12 months after surgery for benign prostatic obstruction?

design.blinding: patient-blinded; surgeons and outcome assessors not masked

arms.label: Thulium laser transurethral vaporesection of the prostate (ThuVARP)

design.population: 410 men at seven UK hospitals with bothersome lower urinary tract symptoms or urinary retention from benign prostatic obstruction who were suitable for TURP; 52% were catheterized at baseline and prostate size was not restricted.
design.description: Pragmatic, patient-blinded, parallel-group equivalence randomized trial
design.locator: Abstract; Methods (study design, randomisation); Results text; Table 1; Figure 1

verdictNote: IPSS was equivalent, but TURP gave a higher Qmax; ThuVARP did not shorten stay or reduce complications.
takeaway: In 410 UK men with benign prostatic obstruction randomized under anesthesia, thulium laser vaporesection (ThuVARP) and TURP were equivalent for IPSS at 12 months, but TURP gave a higher Qmax; hospital stay and complication rates were similar.

reports.label: Primary report (12-month IPSS and Qmax)
reports.citation: Hashim H, Worthington J, Abrams P, et al. "Thulium laser transurethral vaporesection of the prostate versus transurethral resection of the prostate for men with lower urinary tract symptoms or urinary retention (UNBLOCS): a randomised controlled trial." *Lancet.* 2020;396(10243):50-61. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30537-7
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; follow-up completed December 2017

results.measure: Mean IPSS at 12 months (ThuVARP minus TURP, adjusted for centre and baseline diagnosis)
results.note: Equivalence margin 2.5 points; the confidence interval lies inside it. Table 3 gives SDs of 6.79 and 5.79 and a crude difference of 0.16 (95% CI -1.08 to 1.41). 310 of 410 men completed the 12-month IPSS; the primary analysis used multiple imputation. No subgroup interaction (retention versus LUTS, p=0.888).

results.measure: Mean Qmax at 12 months in mL/s (ThuVARP minus TURP, adjusted for centre and baseline diagnosis)
results.note: Equivalence margin 4 mL/s; the lower confidence limit lies outside it, so the procedures were not equivalent, and superiority testing favored TURP. Table 3 gives SDs of 16.88 and 13.28 and a crude difference of -3.08 (95% CI -5.75 to -0.41). Qmax was recorded for 344 of 410 men. Subgroup interaction by retention versus LUTS p=0.189.

results.measure: Median length of hospital stay in hours (IQR); adjusted difference ThuVARP minus TURP
results.note: Analyzed in 198 men per arm. The abstract and Results text describe the 48 h as a mean; Table 5 reports medians.

results.measure: Post-void residual at 12 months, ordinal analysis by quintile (odds ratio ThuVARP versus TURP)

values.exp: 42/169 (25%) in the highest quintile (141 to 1000 mL)
values.ctl: 27/176 (15%) in the highest quintile (141 to 1000 mL)

results.note: Zero residual in 39 (23%) of 169 versus 39 (22%) of 176. Higher residuals with ThuVARP did not reach p<0.05.

results.measure: Nocturia more than once per night at 12 months (odds ratio ThuVARP versus TURP)
results.note: On the ordinal scale of 0 to 5 times per night, p=0.031. Other IPSS storage and voiding subscores did not differ.

results.measure: IIEF total score at 12 months (adjusted difference ThuVARP minus TURP)
results.note: Only 218 of 410 men (53%) returned the IIEF; analyzed in 100 ThuVARP and 118 TURP patients. SDs 7.46 and 7.34.

results.measure: ICIQ satisfaction score at 12 months, 0 to 10 (adjusted difference ThuVARP minus TURP)
results.note: Would have the same treatment again (definitely or probably): 150 (91%) versus 165 (95%).

results.measure: Prostate cancer diagnosed on routine histology of resected tissue (odds ratio ThuVARP versus TURP)
results.note: Exploratory. Median resected tissue weight was 65% lower after ThuVARP than after TURP (7 g versus 20 g).

harms.label: At least one postoperative complication
harms.note: Ordinal analysis of 0, 1 and more than 1 complications: odds ratio 1.10 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.63), p=0.623. More than one complication in 68 (34%) versus 64 (31%). The Results text transposes the two group totals; the abstract and Tables 1 and 5 agree.

harms.label: Transurethral resection syndrome
harms.note: Serum sodium fell by a median of 2 versus 3 mmol/L (p=0.290). Not collected at 3 or 12 months.

harms.label: Bleeding requiring a hemoglobin measurement
harms.locator: Table 4; denominators by summing the grade rows
harms.note: Odds ratio 1.00 (95% CI 0.42 to 2.35), p=0.992. Grade IIIb: 1 versus 1.

harms.label: Clot retention
harms.locator: Table 4; denominators by summing the grade rows
harms.note: Odds ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.30 to 1.79), p=0.498. Grade IIIb: 0 versus 1.

harms.label: Urethral stricture
harms.locator: Table 4; denominators by summing the grade rows
harms.note: Odds ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.45 to 4.59), p=0.546. Grade IIIa 4 (2%) versus 0 and grade IIIb 3 (2%) versus 3 (2%).

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: Table 4; denominators by summing the grade rows
harms.note: Odds ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.67 to 1.55), p=0.938. Grade II 51 (26%) versus 53 (27%); grade IVb 1 versus 0.

harms.label: Indwelling catheter at 12 months
harms.note: Odds ratio 1.95 (95% CI 0.35 to 10.82), p=0.446. At 3 months 5/196 (3%) versus 5/201 (2%). Catheter-free rate 98% at 3 and 12 months across arms.

harms.label: Repeat TURP for obstruction by 12 months
harms.note: Number of men; the report does not give denominators.

harms.label: Reduced or no ejaculation at 12 months
harms.note: Odds ratio 1.13 (95% CI 0.47 to 2.71), p=0.780; at baseline 86% versus 84% of non-catheterized men reported reduced or no ejaculation. Painful ejaculation at 12 months 8 (7%) versus 17 (12%), p=0.179.

harms.label: Change in sexual function after surgery (both arms, men with LUTS)
harms.note: Post hoc. Of 70 men with sexual dysfunction at baseline, 22 (31%) were worse, 32 (46%) unchanged and 16 (23%) improved; 6 of 25 men (24%) without baseline dysfunction developed mild to moderate symptoms.

delivery.label: Procedure received as allocated
delivery.note: 53 ThuVARP-allocated men (26%) did not receive ThuVARP (count by subtraction). Reasons are in the appendix; nine conversions to TURP were attributed to prostate size.

delivery.label: Conversion from ThuVARP to TURP during surgery, by surgeon's first versus second half of cases
delivery.value: 13/94 (14%) in the first half and 22/90 (24%) in the second half
delivery.note: The report found no evidence of a learning-curve effect on conversion.

delivery.label: Technique
delivery.value: ThuVARP used a LISA Revolix 120 W thulium laser with a 550 micrometer fibre, resecting in chips as in TURP; centres used their usual monopolar or bipolar TURP.

delivery.label: Surgeon training and experience
delivery.value: All trial surgeons were trained in ThuVARP and independently assessed before enrolling patients; they had done more than 100 TURPs but 5 to 12 ThuVARPs.

delivery.label: Postoperative catheter time
delivery.note: Hazard ratio for time to catheter removal 1.02 (95% CI 0.83 to 1.26), p=0.830.

delivery.label: Hemoglobin change after surgery
delivery.note: Adjusted difference 0.88 g/L (95% CI -2.14 to 3.89), p=0.568; analyzed in 146 versus 138.

delivery.label: Patient masking
delivery.value: 238 of 342 men (70%) did not know which operation they had at the end of follow-up; 34 (10%) found out accidentally.
delivery.note: Randomization followed induction of anesthesia; surgeons and outcome assessors were not masked.

reports.label: Cost-effectiveness analysis
reports.citation: Noble SM, Ahern AM, Worthington J, et al. "The cost-effectiveness of transurethral resection of the prostate vs thulium laser transurethral vaporesection of the prostate in the UNBLOCS randomised controlled trial for benign prostatic obstruction." *BJU Int.* 2020;126(5):595-603. doi:10.1111/bju.15138

results.measure: Adjusted mean 12-month secondary care cost per patient (difference TURP minus ThuVARP)
results.note: Costs valued with UK reference costs; resource use from hospital records and questionnaires.

results.measure: Adjusted mean QALY difference over 12 months (TURP minus ThuVARP, EQ-5D-5L)
results.note: Favored TURP numerically; the interval includes zero.

results.measure: Probability that TURP is the cost-effective option at £20,000 per QALY
results.note: Probability reported for TURP; the willingness-to-pay threshold is the one used by NICE.

delivery.label: Operative time
delivery.value: The ThuVARP operation took on average 21 minutes longer than TURP.

relations.note: Another randomized comparison of an alternative BPH operation with TURP and a blinded patient-reported symptom endpoint; WATER tested robotic waterjet resection.
